paths.description: Homepage/listing archetype: purpose, search, current content, responsive and global quality signals.
Bollywood category listing, representing category/index templates.
Movie detail and primary download CTA, representing content/detail templates.
External Linkmake handoff reached from the detail CTA; verified available file-size actions without starting a binary download.
No-results search state, representing form feedback and recovery.

findings.summary: The site is hard-coded to a light palette and does not honor dark mode.
findings.evidence: The default and prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshots are byte-for-byte visually identical; the DOM CSS hard-codes white body and table surfaces and declares no color-scheme.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and replace hard-coded surface/text colors with preference-aware custom properties or light-dark().

findings.summary: Full-page navigation swaps abruptly with no view transition.
findings.evidence: The representative home → detail → external handoff journey uses ordinary MPA navigation; DOM/CSS contains no @view-transition rule or view-transition-name.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } and stable view-transition-name values for shared header and poster elements, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: The long listing provides no scroll-position cue or adaptive page chrome.
findings.evidence: Layout measured a 6,144px mobile document while screenshots and CSS show static header/search chrome and no progress, shrinking, or scroll-state treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a lightweight scroll progress or state-aware sticky search/header treatment, implemented declaratively where supported.

findings.summary: Keyword-heavy footer/tag copy overwhelms useful content and adds substantial visual noise.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM includes a 362px repetitive keyword “Tag” block plus repeated Filmy4wap keyword headings and navigation after each template.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove keyword stuffing and collapse repeated boilerplate into concise, semantic footer navigation; retain only content useful to people.

findings.summary: Lab performance is inconsistent and third-party work creates a long main-thread task.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.3s (outside the good ≤2.5s range); the independent trace measured one 569.84ms long task and 519.84ms TBT, despite a 1.50s trace LCP.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the late third-party task, keep LCP media discoverable and high priority, and defer or remove nonessential analytics/ad work until after interaction or idle.

findings.summary: Duplicate analytics code dominates transferred JavaScript.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded three Google tag script downloads totaling about 500KB of the 661KB transfer, including two measurement IDs and a duplicate load of G-464RLQ64D3.
findings.suggestedFix: Load one analytics library once, consolidate measurement configuration, and remove the duplicate/opaque analytics bootstrap.

findings.summary: Text contrast fails WCAG AA in template content.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified “Tag:” at #008000 on #dde7f1 with a 4.1:1 ratio where 4.5:1 is required for 13px bold text.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a darker green or a lighter background and test all dynamically assigned title/tag colors against WCAG AA.

findings.summary: Third-party cookie and browser inspector issues are triggered by the ad script.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse best-practices scored 0.77 and reported five third-party cookies plus cookie Inspector issues from xr.formelamulae.com and redirected opaque domains; HAR also recorded the ad script blocked by ORB.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the opaque ad bootstrap or replace it with a vetted, privacy-preserving integration that produces no cookie/ORB inspector issues.

findings.summary: Essential browser-enforced security headers are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirmed HTTPS but found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive CSP (including frame-ancestors), HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy at the origin/CDN.

findings.summary: Tracking and opaque third parties are loaded before user choice and dominate the page payload.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 7 third-party origins, Google Tag Manager/Analytics, and an opaque ad origin; HAR attributed 660,765 of 661,160 transferred bytes to third parties and Lighthouse observed five third-party cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory and remove nonessential third parties, gate optional analytics/ads behind meaningful consent, and batch/minimise any retained telemetry.

findings.summary: The internationalized page does not mark language changes and uses physical-direction CSS.
findings.evidence: The document declares html lang=en while visible headings include Hindi text without lang=hi; the captured CSS repeatedly uses left/right physical properties and no logical inline/block equivalents.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark Hindi spans/headings with lang="hi", set direction where needed, and migrate layout rules to logical properties such as margin-inline and text-align:start.

findings.summary: Image delivery lacks modern format and responsive-source signals.
findings.evidence: The images primitive classified all 55 images as legacy PNG and found no modern-format images; one image lacked srcset. Dimensions, lazy loading, and displayed sizing were otherwise good.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP with correct Content-Type and use srcset/sizes where display size varies; retain explicit dimensions and lazy loading.

findings.summary: robots.txt advertises a sitemap on an unrelated hostname.
findings.evidence: robots.txt says “Sitemap: https://tvdl.m1link.qzz.io/sitemap.xml” while the working sitemap and canonical pages are on filmyfly.faith.
findings.suggestedFix: Change the robots.txt Sitemap directive to the canonical filmyfly.faith sitemap and keep canonical URLs consistent across templates.

Deploy CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking, referrer, and permissions policies
Fix all dynamic text/background contrast combinations
Remove keyword stuffing and simplify repeated footer chrome
Reduce long tasks and protect LCP from late third-party work
Mark language changes and use logical CSS properties
Add cross-document and scroll-position navigation cues
